text: Localities retain decision-making authority, with a heavier burden of public recordkeeping.
Unified coordination remains subject to citizenship and local capacity to provide for residents.
After relocation, who remains a citizen
Local customs and shared identity are meeting. New residents, operators, and public service workers do not all share the same position.
Equal citizenship
Establishes eligibility for shared laws across regions and voluntary accession.
Retain local identity customs
Retain local identity requirements; other regions may refuse to join or centralize authority.
What should public workshops take on first
Care workers and factory workers can both explain the shortages. The public warehouse holds only actual materials, and workstations cannot be used twice.
Fewer public manufacturing workstations, preserving local capacity.
Commit more workstations and raw materials to public manufacturing.
What should assistive bodies serve first
Long-term caregivers want to treat damaged bodies first; engineers want to open enhancement to volunteers. Modification does not replace consent or safety follow-up.
Treatment first
Keep basic clinical limits and a lower monitoring burden.
Open enhancement to volunteers
Improve the repair capacity of modified people, while increasing consumption of follow-up medication and cultures.
Can synthetic people serve as representatives
The repair shop demands clear accountability; synthetic people and their coworkers demand equal political standing. Supporters and opponents are not limited to any one kind of body.
Grant representative status; genuine synthetic people may hold public office, and it cannot be revoked retroactively.
Guarantee residence and property first
Count them in population and provisions, without automatically granting representation; legislation can follow later.
Keep space for gardens, or for the factory
Ordinary residents and modified people both need everyday life. Either path can reach the maiden voyage.
Ecology and public provisioning
More garden workstations, fewer in the factory; actual materials still have to be paid for.
Prioritize advanced manufacturing
Reduce gardens and expand manufacturing jobs; a lack of health will lead to rejection by public vote.
Mixed rotation
Find a middle ground across the limited workstations available.
Represent one Earth to the outside
The eight regions already share responsibilities. Should their common external representation be established by unified federal law, or by a shared pact binding each locality?
Common federal law
Shared citizenship and external representation, while localities retain their everyday systems and assets.
Retain internal governments, while unifying representation through binding common law and arbitration.
What should the two cities trade first
Lakeside has farmland and wood; the Departure Depot has tools. Medicine and iron each have their own uses. The same shipment cannot be promised twice.
Each shipment: trade 96 tools and 48 medicine for 1200 food and 160 scrap; both sides must still keep enough food for themselves.
Each shipment: trade 160 tools and 24 iron for 1400 food and 80 scrap; this ties up iron that could be used for repairs and construction.
Who should pay the extra share for road repairs
Lakeside also needs to repair its own workshop. Keeping the road running costs wood and tools; covering more of its costs will draw on this city's construction reserves.
Reduce Lakeside's ongoing maintenance burden, with this city covering more actual road materials and transport costs; the agreement requires 6 knowledge from this city.
Continue splitting costs equally
Preserve this city's construction reserves; Lakeside must also keep paying its half. Both cities will halt operations if supplies run short.
Which shipment should get on the train first

Lakeside's food and medicine and Mineridge's tools and materials share limited vehicles. Expanding the depot also takes materials and maintenance; first decide who gets priority with the vehicles on hand.
When both routes can depart, prioritize food and medicine; the other route may yield up to two times, and still needs an actual order.
Prioritize iron and tools; food and medicine may arrive late. The other route may yield up to two times.
Keep alternating dispatch; add no vehicles and make no advance claim on the other city's supplies.
Register the accession agreement first

Withdraw the proposal; institutional expenditures already made and statutory bills will remain as recorded
